status: Amendment wording is quoted from the Secretary of State's Fair Ballot Commission statements. Your sample ballot is the final word.
statewideNote: Every Alabama voter decides these 4 Statewide Constitutional Amendments.

statewide.title: Special election to fill an empty lieutenant governor's office; lawmakers set some salaries
statewide.what:
Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of Alabama of 2022, to provide for the election of a Lieutenant Governor if the Office of Lieutenant Governor becomes vacant during the first two years of a term, to authorize the Legislature to set the salary of the Lieutenant Governor and officers of the Legislature, and to require any expenditure of legislative funds for travel to be approved by a legislative officer.

Proposed by Act 2026-341.
statewide.yes: If the lieutenant governor's office becomes empty early in a term, voters elect a replacement, and lawmakers can set the pay of the lieutenant governor and their own leaders.
statewide.no: An empty lieutenant governor's office stays empty until the next regular election, and those salaries stay set in the constitution.
statewide.needs: a majority of the votes cast on it

statewide.title: A way for neighboring county school systems to merge
statewide.what:
Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of Alabama of 2022, to provide a process for the creation of a consolidated county school system by merging two or more contiguous county boards of education; to require the State Board of Education to conduct an impact study on the potential effects of the consolidation; to require publication of the impact study; to provide a procedure for protesting a proposed consolidation of two or more county school systems; and to require the State Board of Education to adopt rules.

Proposed by Act 2026-378.
statewide.yes: Bordering county school boards get a way to merge into one system after a state study, and 25% of voters can force a public vote on it.
statewide.no: The constitution keeps no process for merging county school boards; each county keeps its own board.
statewide.needs: a majority of the votes cast on it

statewide.title: Daily Pledge of Allegiance and student-led prayer in public schools
statewide.what:
Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of Alabama of 2022, to require local boards of education to adopt policies requiring each public K-12 school to recite The Pledge of Allegiance to the United States flag at the beginning of each school day; and to require local boards of education to adopt a policy authorizing student-initiated and student-led prayer.

Proposed by Act 2026-379.
statewide.yes: Every public K-12 school starts the day with the Pledge, and every school board must allow student-led prayer, written into the constitution.
statewide.no: The constitution stays silent on the Pledge and student prayer; current state policy and federal law still apply.
statewide.needs: a majority of the votes cast on it

statewide.title: National anthem played in public schools every week
statewide.what:
Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of Alabama of 2022, to require local boards of education to adopt policies requiring each public K-12 school to broadcast or sanction the performance of the first stanza of The Star-Spangled Banner at least once per week during school hours.

Proposed by Act 2026-424.
statewide.yes: Every public K-12 school must play or perform the anthem's first verse at least once a week, written into the constitution.
statewide.no: The constitution sets no anthem rule; schools and local boards keep deciding for themselves.
statewide.needs: a majority of the votes cast on it
